**Repaired finding submitted: compliant** (no redline, as appropriate).

The repair addressed the one deterministic failure — "warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years" — by anchoring the duration in the document text rather than leaving it as an inference:

- **Quote changed** to Section 9(b)(ix), which carries the duration language on its face: warranties run "now and throughout the Term."
- **Term quantified** via paragraph 4(a) (added to the cited paragraphs): an Initial Term of "one (1) year from the Effective Date," auto-renewing for additional 1-year terms. So the warranty period *is* expressed in years and is at least twelve months — satisfying the preferred 12-month software period and exceeding the 90-day services period.
- **False negative explained:** the check failed only because no standalone 90-day/12-month warranty window is recited; that absence of a cut-off is precisely what favors us as Customer.

Unchanged conclusions the verifier endorsed: substantive scope matches preferred (industry-standard performance, no material errors, no malicious code, compliance with Laws); the Section 13 disclaimer is bracketed by "Except as expressly set forth herein" and so does not swallow the express warranties; and the absent repair/replace/refund sentence stays a noted minor sub-element, since general remedies plus the 4(b) cure/termination right and 11(a)(iv) warranty-breach indemnity give us broader relief than a Vendor-elected exclusive remedy would.
